overview.summary: A lightweight concept-art browser for SideScroll. Location groups are virtual inside Concept Lab, while every physical project file remains in the repository root so iPhone GitHub uploads can use Select All.
workflow: Keep patch ZIPs physically flat: all files, including concept images, live at the project root.
Concept Lab provides the location grouping virtually, so physical subfolders are not required.
Name new location references with the matching prefix, for example concept-woodland-02.png or concept-wetlands-water-detail-01.png.
Add a new root image filename to the relevant location in Concept Lab so it appears as a support reference.
Write design notes per location inside Concept Lab. Notes autosave on this device and can be exported/imported as JSON.

locations.title: Woodland
locations.summary: Primary side-scrolling forest route. This is the current closest match to the game's camera and platformer framing.
designQuestions: How close is this to the approved in-game camera height and path readability?
What dressing density feels right around traversal spaces?
Which props or puzzle hooks should become part of the woodland baseline?

locations.title: Mountain Trail
locations.summary: Rockier elevated route with a stone bridge and a more mountainous edge, intended as a distinct traversal biome before full snow conditions.
designQuestions: What makes this feel meaningfully different from woodland while still belonging to the same game?
Where should climb points, ledges and bridge puzzles live?
How sharp should the forest-to-mountain transition be?

locations.title: Snowy Mountain Pass
locations.summary: A colder, clearly separate mountain location with snow cover and a stronger high-altitude identity.
designQuestions: How much snow/ice can we support while preserving platform readability?
Should this biome introduce slipping, wind, or other traversal modifiers?
What visual anchors make it distinct from the non-snow mountain trail?

locations.title: Wetlands / Swimming Route
locations.summary: Reed-heavy marshland with a possible above-water and underwater traversal split, suitable for swimming and water-focused puzzles.
designQuestions: How much of the route should be above water versus submerged?
What new mechanics are introduced here: swimming, diving, current, buoyancy?
How sparse should trees become compared with woodland?

images.title: Wetlands crossing above and below water

locations.title: Underground Caves
locations.summary: Subterranean cavern route with a different lighting logic and a more enclosed, puzzle-forward feel.
designQuestions: How dark and mysterious should the cave route be versus maintaining readability?
What environmental mechanics belong here: climb walls, drop shafts, light, crystal/artefact interactions?
How much ruin/terraforming presence should be visible this early?

locations.title: Settlement / Keep Approach
locations.summary: A settlement route that evolves from sparse shacks to a village and then toward a stone-walled keep, still inhabited in feel but strangely empty.
designQuestions: How do we break this biome into outskirts, village core, and keep approach?
What props imply life and use without showing crowds of people?
What puzzles or story beats suit a more built environment?

images.title: Quiet village road to the castle gate

locations.title: Barren Wastes / Sparse Gravel Biome
locations.summary: A more sparse, rocky, almost moonlike route that could become a later distinct biome or feed into a stranger endgame location.
designQuestions: Is this a true biome or just a placeholder for a future final area?
How much alien/terraforming weirdness should be visible here?
What terrain language keeps it readable while feeling sparse and unusual?
